title: Ordering-based Causal Discovery via Generalized Score Matching

problem.claim: Learning DAG structures from purely observational data is a longstanding challenge.

gap.claim: Existing score matching for causal discovery was originally designated for continuous data, leaving a need for extension to discrete data.

contributions.claim: Extends the score matching framework for causal discovery to discrete data.
Introduces a leaf discriminant criterion based on the discrete score function.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the leaf discriminant criterion based on the discrete score function as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Simulated and real-world experiments reportedly demonstrate accurate inference of true causal orders from observed discrete data.
The identified ordering reportedly significantly improves the accuracy of existing causal discovery baselines in most settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Observational DAG structure learning remains challenging.
A research direction first identifies a topological order through leaf-node detection and then prunes edges.
The paper extends score matching to discrete causal discovery and introduces a discrete-score leaf criterion.
Experiments report accurate order inference and improved baseline accuracy in most settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the theoretical conditions or proof details.
